scope: Source-inspection-driven selection between every same-destination stream-copy and re-encode pairing currently certified in the public registry

selectionPolicy: Inspect the selected browser File with bounded source parsers before conversion.
Keep the selected stream-copy profile when every required inspected stream is standards-compliant for that destination.
When copy is blocked, choose a public, passing re-encode profile only when it has the same physical destination family and a certified decoder for the inspected video codec.
If no certified fallback exists, retain the explicit blocker; never rename, silently transcode, or choose an untested decoder.

assertions: H.264/AAC Matroska remains on lossless MKV-to-MP4 stream copy
MPEG-2 Matroska falls back from blocked MP4 copy to certified MPEG-4 Part 2 re-encode
HEVC Matroska falls back from blocked AV1 WebM copy to certified VP8 re-encode
VP9 is not routed into a video specialist that has no certified VP9 decoder
the exhaustive current registry inventory contains exactly the MKV-to-MP4 and MKV-to-WebM copy-plus-encode families

browserGate.focusedCommand: $env:WITHIN_TEST_VIDEO='off'; npx playwright test tests/browser/media-options.spec.ts --grep "bounded inspection automatically" --reporter=line

fallbackCase.initialPlan: blocked because MPEG-2 is outside the certified MP4 copy set

limitations: Automatic fallback can select only a route already public, passing, and certified for the inspected codec; absent combinations remain explicitly blocked and are tracked under M-04.
A heterogeneous-codec batch is not auto-routed from the first file; every item retains native preflight validation and an incompatible item fails before its output is committed.
The current registry has two physical destination families with both copy and encode choices. The unit inventory must change when another family is added.
